props_note: Our own probabilities for these lines appear here once they've been graded against real results.
notes: Market fair is the books' price on both sides with the hold removed, averaged across the books quoting the most common line.
A fair number needs two books pricing both sides of a prop (three books for anytime TD). Until then the prop shows its best price only.
Best is the best price any book we check posts at that line, as of when the lines were pulled. Prices move, so check the book before you bet.
Our projections are averages. Yardage finishes are lopsided, so a typical game lands below the average: a receiver projected for 60 yards clears 60 less than half the time.
Anytime TD is posted one way (yes only), so its market number is the average across books with their cut still in it. It runs higher than the true chance.

The defense numbers are what that defense allowed per game to the players it faced at the position, over its own games in the window you pick, ranked against every defense. The colors read from the player's side: green when the defense is in the top third for giving up that stat, red in the bottom third, yellow in between. Sacks, interceptions and takeaways flip, since those are the defense's own plays. Early in a season the numbers rest on a couple of games. Our projections don't adjust for the opponent: when we tested that, it didn't help.

Air yards count how far past the line of scrimmage a pass traveled, caught or not. aDOT is air yards per target, YAC is yards after the catch, CPOE is completion rate above what each throw's difficulty predicts, and EPA is expected points added.
Research, not picks: no edge, no lean, no bet recommended.
